authority.alpha_prerequisite: Complete the next bounded D-01 prerequisite by making the existing sealed RrdEngine installation the only successful product startup authority, proving deterministic same-plan recovery at every pre-locator interruption, and directly removing the conflicting pre-canonical development manifest, initializer, security-bootstrap, raw CLI, and supervisor success paths without inventing a migration or compatibility product line.

current_behavior: At clean baseline d179a4e, whose only changes from source baseline 57838e4 are the D01-04 v1 through v4 planning records, RrdEngine already plans a deterministic project-local estate and atomically commits the initial memory seat, complete security state, audit record, installed record, configuration, checkpoint, attunement plan, and pending attunement job before publishing .rrflow/config.toml. A successful replay with an existing locator is exact. A process interruption before locator publication is not recoverable: retry rejects the partial .rrflow tree and can strand randomly generated token and operator credentials. Product and fixture callers can also bypass installation through tracked .rrflow/instance.toml, InstanceManifest and InstanceBinding, ProjectAuthorityBinding, open_project_store/open_bound, rrd-server initialize, rrd-security-bootstrap, rrflow dev supervision, raw primary-CLI operations, MCP embedded create/open, SDK fixtures, local deployment preparation, and two Kubernetes init paths. Complete conformance review found that the v1 plan omitted the checked SDK corpus whose literal pre-canonical instance identity conflicts with the deterministic identity produced by canonical installation. Implementation review then proved that removing dependencies from rrflow-cli/Cargo.toml necessarily changes its Cargo.lock package entry, contrary to the frozen-lock stop condition, and an MCP boundary test exposed ContextPacket JSON round-trip digest instability when a lexical f64 score is reparsed. Documentation validation additionally found two supporting records that link directly to files deleted by the cutover: the historical platform-vocabulary note links runtime/instance.rs, and the seat-identity reference presents the removed raw CLI commands/test as its executable surface. Final product-source review then found an undeclared `RrdEngine::open` in `EngineLocalBackupDriver`: it targets the pre-canonical `.rrflow/rrd` parent, where create-or-open semantics could manufacture a second empty store instead of failing on the canonical installed `roots/<install-id>` topology. The repository-local ignored .rrflow/rrd tree contains existing development data and is not a migration target or disposable fixture.
target_behavior: The exact sealed installation plan becomes the only successful product creation boundary. Apply creates an owner-only, versioned, plan-addressed installation intent after all no-write validation, records the first accepted apply time, resumes only the same target/profile/executable/configuration/project precondition, reuses one token and one plan-bound operator credential, distinguishes an empty engine from the exact atomic installed commit, publishes a missing locator after full readback, and removes only its own bounded intent. Foreign, malformed, symlinked, ambiguous, partially committed, differently sealed, or pre-existing unowned .rrflow state fails closed without rewrite or deletion. The primary rrflow CLI exposes only version, install plan/apply, serve, authenticated ready, and read-only verify from the currently implemented product lifecycle. MCP embedded mode, the standalone internal server process, conformance fixtures, local-process deployment input, and Kubernetes rendering open or apply the same installed estate. The SDK corpus binds one deterministic installed identity derived from an empty project and a versioned test-only distribution anchor; the harness asserts that identity before seeding and all six language clients consume the same unchanged corpus. The pre-canonical manifest, private project binding, standalone security bootstrap, initializer, development supervisor, and raw primary-CLI success surfaces are deleted after replacement tests pass. The retained application-backup driver uses open-existing semantics so the pre-canonical parent path cannot silently become a second empty store; canonical installed backup resolution remains explicitly blocked for its later owning package. Supporting documentation links to the canonical topology/change evidence and engine-owned seat/warp behavior instead of deleted source or CLI tests. The CLI package description reflects that product surface while lock-bound unused dependency declarations remain unchanged for a dedicated lock-maintenance package. The verified ContextPacket round-trip defect is added to POAM-015 without altering its contract, digest, or acceptance semantics in this lifecycle package.
unchanged_behavior: README remains the identity/current-status owner, the alpha objective remains the measurable outcome owner, the roadmap remains the only gate-status owner, and the POA&M remains the open-deficiency ledger.
Version 1.0.0 remains frozen. This package does not create a release, tag, artifact, promotion, or push and does not authorize the official rrflow/rrflow remote.

D-01 and OBJ-07 remain partial after this prerequisite. Repair, restore, uninstall, signed offline distribution, platform ACL qualification, hostile ancestor replacement, full attunement execution, and final release proof remain open.

POAM-006, POAM-016, POAM-020, POAM-021, and POAM-024 remain active. The local-process driver private state/marker redesign, estate controller binaries, Kubernetes reconciliation/readiness/deletion/RBAC qualification, duplicate estate topology, and operation-specific resource grammar are not closed here.

The ignored repository-local .rrflow/rrd, .rrflow/dev, and .rrflow/verification data is user development state. Implementation may remove only the tracked .rrflow/instance.toml file and must not read, migrate, rename, truncate, clean, or delete any ignored .rrflow bytes.

A pre-existing unowned or pre-canonical .rrflow tree remains a collision. The installer reports it and stops; there is no compatibility reader, automatic migration, fallback root, alias, or cleanup mode.

RrdEngine remains the provider-neutral composition and durable-effect boundary. Explicit raw engine construction may remain only as a component-test/internal composition seam; product executables and adapters may not use it as a creation or lifecycle authority.

Security vocabulary and direct component characterization may remain, but initial installed policy, principal, credential hash, audit, checkpoint, and attunement job are still created in the one atomic installation commit.

Adaptive exploratory reasoning remains fluid under ADR-0002. This package adds no schema of thought, reasoning workflow, DataFusion executor, automatic tuning decision, external provider dependency, or Connectome lifecycle authority.
The existing local-process kill matrix remains fault-injection evidence for process effect gaps, not a real-world product-readiness or performance test. It is not used to claim this package accepted.
The SDK conformance installation anchor is inert, versioned test input only. It is not a distributable RRFlow executable, signed bundle, product installation proof, or release qualification.

ContextPacket floating-point wire normalization and digest redesign are not lifecycle work. The observed round-trip mismatch remains explicit in POAM-015 and no digest check or test expectation is weakened here.

Dependencies used only by removed rrflow-cli source remain declared until a separately planned Cargo.lock maintenance change can remove their lock entry; no surviving product code may import or execute them.
No Cargo.lock change is planned. If dependency resolution changes, implementation stops and authors a separately bound plan revision before proceeding.

runtime_trace.reason: Add bounded installation stage/recovery observations carrying operation, plan SHA-256, non-secret installed identity, stage, recovery classification, idempotent-replay flag, elapsed time, and file/byte counts. Preserve existing trace vocabulary and redact secrets, absolute project content, and private reasoning.

resource_evidence.reason: Record per-failpoint created/reused/removed owned files and bytes, final physical inspection, exactly one token hash and credential hash, and zero modifications to collision fixtures. This package changes no hot query/storage algorithm, so throughput promotion benchmarks are not acceptance evidence.

debugging_evidence.reason: Add a typed, test-only installation failpoint/probe at each durable boundary and preserve intermediate artifacts for assertion. No environment-variable backdoor, hidden release hook, sleep-based scheduler oracle, or runtime lifecycle switch may ship.

first_failure_oracle: Before implementation, the recovery test injected after storage creation must fail on retry because apply rejects the partial .rrflow tree; the same test becomes green only when the exact plan resumes without replacing token or credential material.

Before removal, the architecture scan finds tracked .rrflow/instance.toml plus InstanceManifest, InstanceBinding, ProjectAuthorityBinding, ensure_dedicated, open_project_store/open_bound, rrd-server initialize, rrd-security-bootstrap, rrflow dev, and duplicate Kubernetes bootstrap callers in production/product paths; after cutover it finds none, without confusing MCP protocol initialization or component-only security repository initialization.

For every injected durable boundary, the first apply returns the typed injected failure and a second apply of the same plan converges to the same validated result with one runtime commit, one security state, one installation audit/checkpoint/job set, one token hash, one credential hash, and one locator; a different plan, executable, project precondition, malformed intent, link, unknown file, partial control state, or forged digest is rejected without mutation.

A byte inventory of a pre-existing unowned .rrflow collision fixture is identical before and after plan, apply, retry, open, and verify attempts. The repository-local ignored .rrflow data is never used as a fixture or command target.

The real rrflow binary plans without writes, applies, survives one injected interruption/retry, serves an installed estate, completes authenticated ready/session/commit/reopen/read-only verify, and exposes no removed dev/raw command. The internal rrd-server binary cannot initialize and refuses absent or digest-mismatched installed state before listener publication.

The SDK harness plans a canonical fresh installation from the versioned inert anchor, fails before seeding if the planned instance or estate differs from the checked corpus, opens the installed estate, and the unchanged corpus passes the real daemon protocol suite in Rust, TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, and .NET.

The lexical ContextPacket constructed by the engine is valid before transport but can fail its own packet digest after serde_json f64 round-trip; the installed MCP fixture uses a wire-stable seed case, the mismatch is recorded in POAM-015, and this package neither rounds the score nor weakens validation.

The generated Kubernetes Pod has exactly one installation init container invoking rrflow install apply with the sealed plan digest, no rrd-server initialize or rrd-security-bootstrap command, no caller-selected bootstrap time/credential/instance identity, and a main process that opens the installed estate; renderer tests make no controller/readiness qualification claim.

Documentation validation resolves every local link after the deleted source/test paths are removed; the historical note points to canonical topology/evidence and seat identity names only implemented engine operations/tests while keeping the absent public CLI specialization explicit.

The retained EngineLocalBackupDriver no longer calls create-or-open on the pre-canonical .rrflow/rrd parent. Its existing component fixture still opens and backs up through open_existing, while an absent or canonical roots/<install-id> layout cannot be turned into a second empty store; canonical installed backup resolution remains open work.

stop_conditions: Any implementation or evidence edit exists before the planning-only commit, the worktree baseline is not clean, the plan validator cannot bind the exact revision/tree/digests, or the planning commit changes any second path.

Any reviewed production caller, fixture, generator, checked artifact, or dependency affected by the cutover is missing from this path set; update planning in a new planning-only package rather than editing undeclared files.

Recovery would require guessing ownership, accepting a different sealed plan/input/time, overwriting a file, minting a second token or credential, replaying the initial semantic/security commit, tolerating partial control state, or deleting/moving any unbound .rrflow byte.

A failure point exposes a physical engine state that cannot be classified as absent, exact empty owned store, exact committed installed state, or exact complete locator replay. Preserve evidence and stop for a separately researched storage recovery design.

Removing a pre-canonical file would discard behavior not yet covered by the canonical install, engine, server, client, or component-test replacement. Keep the deletion blocked until the smallest replacement test is green.
An outward executable or adapter still needs InstanceManifest, private ProjectAuthorityBinding, raw-root create/open, standalone security bootstrap, or a compatibility reader to start successfully.

The Kubernetes renderer change would require the controller to assert engine completion, mint credentials, calculate identity, or become a second installer; leave broader POAM-024 work for its own package.

The local-process caller change would require redesigning private process state, markers, fencing, authenticated receipts, deletion, or controller binaries. Keep POAM-021 open and schedule that separately.

Scope expands into repair/restore/uninstall, signed bundle assembly, platform ACL certification, full attunement executors, reasoning-tree execution, Arrow/DataFusion work, storage-performance thresholds, Connectome code, or provider-specific lifecycle.

Scope expands into changing ContextPacket numeric encoding/digests or pruning lock-bound dependency declarations; retain the verified deficiency and schedule each under its owning contract or lock-maintenance package.

The backup correction would require guessing the installed storage root, bypassing locator/executable binding, changing backup controller inputs, or claiming canonical backup support. Stop after replacing create-or-open with fail-closed open-existing and leave installed backup resolution to its owning package.
Any active owner would be made to claim D-01, OBJ-07, a listed POA&M, Gate J, release readiness, or promotion complete from this prerequisite.
Cargo.lock, product version 1.0.0, official remote state, ignored repository-local .rrflow data, or any path outside the declared implementation/evidence set changes.
